landing.title: Which reporting duties apply to your company?
landing.intro: Germany, Austria and Switzerland have introduced new cyber-incident reporting regimes (NIS2UmsuCG, NISG 2024, ISG). We automatically assess which regimes apply to you, which thresholds are relevant, and where your public-facing security gaps are – in under three minutes, no login required.
landing.disclaimer_short: Automated public-footprint assessment – not legal advice.

limits.body: This report was generated automatically: an automated evaluation of publicly available sources (DNS, TLS, HTTP headers, published web pages) combined with your answers. It is a first orientation and **not legal advice**. A full compliance assessment requires internal system information that we cannot see. Legal standing and confidence are shown per regime; uncertain legal situations are honestly reported as “unclear”.

result.title: Incident triage
result.none_relevant: No regime was flagged as relevant based on the country of main establishment alone. Check subsidiaries and sector via the free scan if needed.
result.limits_body: This triage was generated automatically from your incident intake and the versioned YAML rules (NIS2UmsuCG, NISG, ISG). Absolute deadlines are calculated from the stated time of discovery. Without sector and size data the home regime often remains **unclear** – that is intentional. Significance triggers (availability, personal data, scale) come from each rules file. This is a first orientation and **not legal advice**. When in doubt, contact counsel and the competent authority immediately.
result.disclaimer_footer: Automated incident triage · not legal advice · save this link – access is token-based

problem.title: DACH reporting rules are expanding — unevenly
problem.lead: Germany's NIS2UmsuCG, Austria's NISG 2024 and Switzerland's ISG each set their own thresholds, sectors and clocks. One incident can trigger different duties — or none.
problem.emphasis: Most companies only discover which rules apply after the 24-hour reporting window has already started.
points: Three regimes, three thresholds, three timelines
Thresholds mix headcount, revenue and sector lists
Orientation after an incident is too late — the clock has already started

steps.title: Tell us about your company
steps.body: Your domain and a short questionnaire — sector, size, locations, EU customers. About two minutes.

steps.title: We analyse
steps.body: NexusScope maps your profile against all three regimes and checks your public footprint (DNS, TLS, web headers) for visible gaps.

steps.title: You get one unified report
steps.body: Per-regime status, reporting deadlines, a prioritised gap list and the reasoning behind every conclusion — in plain language.

items.q: Does NIS2 / NISG / ISG apply to my company?
items.a: It depends on sector, size and structure — the thresholds differ between Germany, Austria and Switzerland. NexusScope checks your profile against each regime and tells you where you stand, including what remains unclear.

No. NexusScope is an automated orientation based on public sources and your answers. It shows reasoning and confidence levels and clearly marks uncertainty. For binding decisions, consult legal counsel.
Your data is stored in Switzerland and the EU, used only for your report and to notify you about early access. We scan only public sources, honour robots.txt and never access protected systems.
We are onboarding the waitlist for early access now. Join the waitlist and we will let you know as soon as your company can run its first scan.
